title: Pricing Intelligence: Task-Based Learning and Labor Displacement in the AI Economy
abstract: arXiv:2608.11112v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: What determines the speed of labor displacement through AI? I study this question in a microeconomic model in which AI providers sell access to users who must each complete a set of tasks using AI or labor. Users differ in the share of complex tasks they face. Using AI on complex tasks improves AI's ability to perform them. When AI initially has a comparative advantage in easy tasks, users with many complex tasks have low willingness to pay for AI. This creates a tension between profit maximization and complex-task learning. I characterize when this tension gives rise to a convex technological takeoff or a learning trap. Symmetric competition can slow adoption relative to monopoly when weak, but accelerates it when sufficiently intense by shifting usage toward more complex tasks. Asymmetric competition can further accelerate adoption by inducing endogenous specialization among providers.

translated_title: 定价智能：AI经济中的任务型学习与劳动力替代
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.11112v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：什么决定了AI导致劳动力替代的速度？我在一个微观经济模型中研究这个问题，其中AI提供商向用户出售访问权限，每个用户必须使用AI或劳动力完成一组任务。用户面临复杂任务的份额各不相同。在复杂任务上使用AI会提高AI执行这些任务的能力。当AI最初在简单任务上具有比较优势时，面临许多复杂任务的用户对AI的支付意愿较低。这在利润最大化和复杂任务学习之间产生了张力。我刻画了这种张力何时导致凸性技术起飞或学习陷阱。对称竞争在较弱时可能相对于垄断减缓采用，但在足够激烈时通过将使用转向更复杂的任务而加速采用。非对称竞争可以通过诱导提供商之间的内生专业化进一步加速采用。
tldr: 本文通过微观经济模型揭示了AI提供商在利润最大化与复杂任务学习之间的张力如何决定劳动力替代速度，并指出竞争强度和非对称性可通过任务专业化加速AI采用。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals how the tension between profit maximization and complex-task learning in AI provision determines labor displacement speed, showing that competition intensity and asymmetry can accelerate adoption through task specialization.
